item.title: Rabuka confident in People's Alliance support and to form Govt outright on their own
item.description: The People's Alliance is hoping to secure more than 50 percent of the votes at the next general elections to form a government on its own, with its leader expressing confidence in the party's support. Prime Minister and People's Alliance leader Sitiveni Rabuka says he is very confident in the support of his party as it prepares for the next general elections.
item.content:encoded:
The People's Alliance is hoping to secure more than 50 percent of the votes at the next general elections to form a government on its own, with its leader expressing confidence in the party's support.

Prime Minister and People's Alliance leader Sitiveni Rabuka says he is very confident in the support of his party as it prepares for the next general elections.

Rabuka says he has left the selection of candidates entirely to the party's selection committee.

He says the committee had given him the option of indicating whether he wanted his current 20 running mates to contest again, and he had expressed his wish for all of them to stand.

However, Rabuka says the candidates also have the option of stepping down if they feel they no longer wish to contest.

On the party's chances of securing enough votes to form a government on its own, Rabuka acknowledges that it did not receive more than 50 percent of the votes in the previous general election.

He says the party will have to work towards increasing its support and securing as many votes as possible.

Rabuka says if the People's Alliance manages to secure more than 50 percent of the votes, it would have the right to govern on its own.

item.title: National government announcement on drought situation this Friday
item.description: The Government is preparing to make a national announcement this Friday outlining its plans to address the drought situation. Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica , who chaired cabinet today, says the drought situation was among the issues discussed during today's Cabinet meeting.
item.content:encoded:
The Government is preparing to make a national announcement this Friday outlining its plans to address the drought situation.

Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica , who chaired cabinet today, says the drought situation was among the issues discussed during today's Cabinet meeting.

Kamikamica says Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka is expected to make a formal announcement later this week, with the current plan on making the national announcement on Friday.

He says further details on the Government's plans will be provided during the Prime Minister's announcement.

When asked about the Cabinet meeting and the decisions made, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says the public will have to wait for the Cabinet Office to release the decisions.

Rabuka says the release will depend on what Cabinet has decided.

Kamikamica also confirmed that when the Prime Minister is unavailable to attend a Cabinet meeting , one of the Deputy Prime Ministers normally chairs the meeting.

item.title: 46-year-old water source becomes lifeline for Yasawa Village
item.description: Members of Yasawa Village are cleaning and relying on a water source dug in 1980 as prolonged dry weather leaves household water tanks and nearby creeks dry. Speaking to fijivillage News, Viliame Misianini says families are using the old water source for bathing, washing clothes and cleaning dishes as they struggle with the ongoing water shortage.
item.content:encoded:
Members of Yasawa Village are cleaning and relying on a water source dug in 1980 as prolonged dry weather leaves household water tanks and nearby creeks dry.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Viliame Misianini says families are using the old water source for bathing, washing clothes and cleaning dishes as they struggle with the ongoing water shortage.

Misianini says the water source was dug in 1980 by a teacher from Yasawa known as Mr Sakaraia and has never dried up, even during previous periods of prolonged dry weather.

He says although the source has not been used regularly for many years, villagers turn to it whenever they experience severe water shortages.

Misianini says young men and other members of the community are now working together to clean the water source so families can continue using it.

He says villagers have also built thatched bathing shelters near the water source to provide privacy and make it easier for women to bathe and carry out their daily washing.

Insert: Misianini on old watersource. 10th Nov, 2026

Misianini says the situation is particularly difficult for women who need water for washing clothes, dishes and other household activities.

He says the water tanks and nearby creeks have dried up, leaving families dependent on the old water source and occasional rainfall.

Misianini says even a little rain provides some relief, allowing families to collect rainwater for drinking.

Despite the challenges, he says villagers remain united and are doing whatever they can to support one another through the water shortage.

Meanwhile, Misianini says government water assistance has already been delivered to Yasawa Island on two occasions, but Yasawa Village has yet to receive a delivery.

He says the villagers have been informed that water assistance is expected to reach them this week.

Misianini says villagers have already cleaned and prepared their water tanks in anticipation of the delivery.

He says families remain hopeful that the assistance will arrive as expected and provide much-needed relief from the prolonged dry conditions.
